segments.text: Euclid's Elements, Book One, Proposition Fifteen. Intersecting lines make their vertical angles equal. Given segments A B and C D intersecting at point E, we prove that vertical angle A E C equals angle D E B, and angle C E B equals angle A E D.

segments.text: Since segment A E stands on segment C D, Proposition Thirteen shows that the adjacent angles C E A and A E D equal two right angles. Again, since segment D E stands on segment A B, the adjacent angles A E D and D E B also equal two right angles.

subsegments.text: Since segment A E stands on segment C D, Proposition Thirteen shows that the adjacent angles C E A and A E D equal two right angles. Again, since segment D E stands on segment A B, the adjacent angles A E D and D E B also equal two right angles.

segments.style: speaking briskly, nimble, crisp, and composed
segments.text: Because all right angles are equal by Postulate Four, the sum of angles C E A and A E D equals the sum of angles A E D and D E B. Subtracting the common angle A E D from each leaves angle C E A equal to angle B E D. By the same reasoning, angle C E B equals angle D E A. Therefore intersecting lines make their vertical angles equal, as was required to prove.
